## RCA (rebar-debug Phase 1 — confirmed at runtime)

**Mechanism.** One line: `src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py:63`

    lo = max(1, line_start)
    hi = line_end if line_end and line_end >= lo else len(lines)

The `else` branch is the tool's documented "read to EOF" fallback for `line_end == 0`, but the
guard that selects it, `line_end and line_end >= lo`, is false for **two disjoint** inputs: the
documented sentinel (`line_end == 0`) and a **malformed inverted range** (`0 < line_end < lo`,
or a negative `line_end`). Both therefore land on `len(lines)`. An agent that asks for a bounded
window whose end precedes its start is silently handed the whole rest of the file, capped at
`_READ_MAX_LINES`, with nothing in the return value distinguishing that from the window it asked
for.

**Runtime confirmation.** Driving the real closure (40-line fixture, py3.12, worktree at
63db6ac5a8):

```
read_file("f.txt", 5, 8)   -> 4 lines:  "5\tline5" … "8\tline8"          (normal window, correct)
read_file("f.txt", 15, 8)  -> 26 lines: "15\tline15" … "40\tline40"      (INVERTED -> silent EOF)
read_file("f.txt", 38, 0)  -> 3 lines:  "38\tline38" … "40\tline40"      (documented sentinel, correct)
```

The middle row is the defect, observed executing: a request for an 8-line-ending window returned
everything to end of file, with no error and no marker. This is the same shape the ticket
reported live — `read_file(<path>, line_start=115, line_end=30)` issued 31 times by the looping
verifier in bf31, each returning the same ~11,000-char blob.

The third row is the discriminator: it rules out the rival explanation that the `else` branch is
simply mis-guarded in general, or that `lo`'s `max(1, …)` clamp is at fault. The documented
`line_end == 0` sentinel behaves exactly as specified, so the defect is precisely and only the
**inverted** case sharing that branch.

**Legitimacy: `defect`.** The behaviour violates a cited, deliberate, and very recent contract in
this same module:
* commit **85805e02f1** ("bf31: search_files must not fake `(no matches)`", 2026-08-05) fixed
  exactly this class in the sibling tool — "telling the agent a literal is absent when it was
  never looked for" — and its remedy is the one this ticket asks for: "a path that is neither
  file nor directory returns an explicit `Error: …`".
* the invariant is written into the tool contract the agent is given, at
  `pai_tools.py:100-105`: search_files returns "`(no matches)` when the text is genuinely
  absent, or `Error: …` when `path` cannot be searched — **an error is never reported as
  `(no matches)`**".
* bf31's commit message records why it matters here specifically: these are the read-only tools
  every rebar LLM gate hands its agent, and a gate that SIGNS its verdict can be driven to a
  false verdict by a tool that answers a request it did not perform.

This ticket was created as a deliberate scope carve-out from that fix, by its author, to keep
bf31's review surface to one function.

**Caller-dependency gate: clear.** `read_file` is a closure built by `filesystem_tools` and
handed to Pydantic AI agents (`pai_tools.py:167`). Its only in-repo references are the tool-name
memoization set (`agent_call.py:39`), the prompt text describing it (`operations.py:212-215`),
and reviewer prompt docs. No code branches on the return value's shape, and nothing depends on
an inverted range meaning EOF — the callers are LLM agents, for whom the current behaviour is
the harm, not a contract.

**Fix size:** the change is ~5 non-test lines, far below the 150-line non-test floor of the
Gerrit bugfix-size attestation gate (`src/rebar/llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py:3`), so no
plan-review attestation is required for this change.

# `read_file` silently reads to EOF when `line_end < line_start`

Discovered while root-causing [rebar:bf31-fd55-d28d-4b7a] and deliberately left out of that fix's
scope to keep its review surface to one function.

`read_file` (`src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py`) computes
`hi = line_end if line_end and line_end >= lo else len(lines)`. An INVERTED range — `line_end`
below `line_start` — therefore falls back to "read to EOF" (capped at `_READ_MAX_LINES`) rather
than reporting that the request was malformed. The agent asked for a 30-line window and silently
received a 259-line one.

Observed live: the looping verifier in bf31 issued
`read_file(<path>, line_start=115, line_end=30)` **31 times**, each returning the same 11,000-char
blob. The malformed range was not the cause of that loop, but it is the same class of defect as the
one bf31 fixed — a tool answering a request it did not actually perform, with no signal that it
substituted something else.

Note the deliberate, documented case that must be preserved: `line_end=0` means "read to EOF" and is
part of the tool's contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `read_file` with `line_end < line_start` (and `line_end != 0`) returns an explicit `Error: ...`
      naming the malformed range, instead of silently reading to EOF
- [ ] `line_end == 0` still means "read to EOF, capped" — the documented behaviour is unchanged
      (regression pinned)
- [ ] a normal `line_start <= line_end` window is unchanged
- [ ] the docstring states the malformed-range behaviour, since Pydantic AI passes it to the agent
      as the tool contract (`src/rebar/llm/pai_tools.py:46`)
compiled_state.title: read_file silently reads to EOF when line_end < line_start instead of reporting the malformed range
